flags.champions.enabled: default false: champion.put/start/archive/delete refuse with capability_missing; list/get answer (empty); the snapshot carries no champions table. On: the verbs work, snapshot.champions is present, champion.put/champion.deleted deltas flow
flags.champions.homeSync: default false. On: every turn end of an incarnation bundles its home (tar + zstd, files over cells.retention.wipMaxFileBytes skipped) into <transcripts.segments.storeDir>/blobs/champion-homes/<sha256>, one pointer row per new bundle; champion.start on a fresh home restores the newest bundle or the given homeRef before the first runtime
flags.champions.homesDir: <data-dir>/champions by default; where champion.put without home creates the home

schema.mirror: snapshot.champions (flag on), MIRROR_CHAMPION_AUDIT_KINDS champion.put / champion.deleted with MIRROR_CHAMPION_KEYS; champion_home_object.put informational

surfaces: verbs champion.put / champion.get / champion.list / champion.start / champion.archive / champion.delete (capability champions.v1)
bee tags apiary:champion=<id> and apiary:role=champion on the incarnation (Apiary's championIdFromTags keeps working)
env HIVE_CHAMPION_ID / HIVE_CHAMPION_HOME on the incarnation
residentLifecycle: archive/delete of a bee that is the current incarnation of an unarchived Champion are invalid_request (use champion.archive); champion.archive archives the incarnation and keeps identity and home; champion.delete removes the row only; stop/revive and mail wakes work as for any bee; champion.start on a stopped incarnation revives it, on a live one is a no-op plus the optional prompt

gates.registryJsonGone: Honeybee side: identity (id, name, agent, home, template, model, effort, current incarnation, archived) and home bundles live in champions / champion_home_objects; Apiary keeps bio, avatar, scope, pilot settings on Home and reads Honeybee's rows (registry read-only one release) — Apiary's half, mailed to the lead
gates.survivesExecutorSwap: champions.1: executor A runs the Champion, a turn writes MEMORY.md and memory/lab.md, the turn end bundles the home into the shared object directory; A is SIGKILLed; executor B (fresh data dir, own homesDir) champion.put + champion.start {homeRef} restores the bundle before the first runtime (homeRestored true), the incarnation reads its memory (cat MEMORY.md), the pointer is recorded on B; without homeRef B starts from the stub (the pointer is the Home's to hand over)
gates.homeImmutable: champion.put that changes home or agent is invalid_request; champion.delete leaves MEMORY.md in place
gates.bundleCost: .proof/h-track/h5/bundle-measure.json: 2051 files / 7.5 MB tar -> 35 KB zstd in 2.4 s, restore 1.0 s, oversize file skipped and reported, identical home -> identical ref (no new row)

notProven: Apiary consuming champions end to end (its half: mirror the rows, drop registry.json writes, hand homeRef over on a swap)
S3/R2 object store: directory store only, shared between executors by a shared directory in the test
bundle cost on a very large home (bounded by tar + zstd throughput; the 64 MiB per-file cap applies)
orphan sweep of champion-home objects (the H4 transcript sweep covers only blobs/transcript-archives)

leadFindings.1_secrets: bundleChampionHome walks the home first and refuses (reason=secrets, paths logged, up to 20) when any credential-like file is present: .env*, *.pem/*.key/*.p12/*.pfx/*.jks/*.keystore/*.secret/*.token, .netrc/.npmrc/.pypirc/.yarnrc*/.git-credentials, auth.json, credentials*, id_rsa and friends, token/tokens.json/secrets.json, anything under .ssh/.gnupg/.aws/.kube/.docker/.config/gcloud, .claude/*credential*, .codex/auth.json; champions.homeSyncIncludeSecrets (default false) bundles anyway; contract doc says so; champions.1 plants a .env and sees the refusal and no bundle until it is removed
leadFindings.2_epochFence: champions.epoch + fenced_at and champion_home_objects.epoch (v54 DDL edited before any deploy); champion.start {homeRef, epoch} takes epoch+1 (a handover older than the row is champion_fenced, a new closed error code); bundles carry the row epoch; restores skip bundles older than the row epoch (restore_skipped reason=stale_epoch); new verb champion.fence {id, epoch}: the Home tells the stale executor, which takes the epoch, stops a live incarnation, stops bundling (push_skipped reason=fenced) and refuses champion.start with champion_fenced until a newer handover; champions.1 restarts the killed executor, fences it at epoch 1 and proves start / older handover / older fence all refuse
leadFindings.3_orphanSweep: ChampionHomeSync.sweepOrphans runs the shared worker sweep over blobs/champion-homes with the pointer refs, daily in the same tick as transcript objects (and alone when segments are off); deleteChampion already removed pointer rows (no FK, done in the same tx); champions.1 plants a 3 h old orphan and sees it swept while referenced bundles stay
leadFindings.4_restoreSkippedLog: restoreChampionHome logs restore_skipped with reason home_not_empty | no_bundle | stale_epoch before returning
leadFindings.5_templateBinding: template.delete refuses (invalid_request naming the Champions) while a Champion binds the template; champion.start with a bound template that no longer exists refuses instead of spawning argless; champions.1 covers both
leadFindings.6_nodeId: store.nodeId() mints a uuid once into meta.node_id; the WIP scope is that id (hostname only as the sanitising fallback); store.wipNodeScopes remembers every scope this store used; the sweep drops stale refs under any of them and, for unscoped refs, drops those of this store's dead Cells (any row incl. removed) and migrates live ones; wip.0 covers an old prefix, a dead unscoped ref and a foreign unscoped ref
leadFindings.7_walkInWorker: the walk, secrets scan, tar, zstd and the torn check run in the transcript segment worker (kind bundleHome); the daemon thread only inserts the pointer row
leadFindings.nits: comment lines removed from mirror.ts, protocol.ts, types.ts, provision.ts and the misplaced one in store.ts (the SCHEMA_VERSION history block keeps its house-style version notes); torn bundles: the walk fingerprint (path, size, mtime) is compared before and after the tar and a changed home discards the object (reason=torn); every skipped-over-cap path is logged (up to 20)
